items.text: The lower ECAM display shows ENG page
Engines 1 and 2 are usually started first (Engine 2 powers blue hydraulic system, which pressurizes the parking brake).
Do not turn MASTER switch ON before all amber crosses and messages have disappeared on the engine parameters (upper ECAM display).
Wait until the ENG 1 N2 is at about 10 % before switching the ENG 2 MASTER switch at ON (to permit correct operation of the No Break Power Transfer).
ON ECAM UPPER DISPLAY | ON ECAM LOWER DISPLAY

N2 increases | Corresponding start valve in line
 | Bleed pressure indication green
 | Oil pressure increases
At 16 % N2: | Indication of active igniter (A or B) appears

At 22 % N2:
- FF increases
10 seconds (maximum) after fuel is on:
- EGT increases
- N1 increases

At 50 % N2: | Start valve crossline
 | Igniter is turned OFF
At ISA sea level: N1 about 20% N2 about 60% EGT about 400°C FF 300 kg/h (660 lb/h)

items.text: If Autobrake is selected:
If no braking:
If needed, the flight crew may keep maximum reverse thrust until full aircraft stop
Limit brake pressure to approximately 1 000 PSI. Monitor brake pressure on the BRAKES PRESS indicator
If still no braking:
Use short successive parking brake applications to stop the aircraft.
If A/THR not active:
When descent established:
If structural damage suspected:
If CAB ALT above 14 000 ft:
In case of lack of pitch down authority, reducing thrust may be necessary
When out of stall (no longer stall indications):
If in clean configuration and below 20 000 ft:
At the same time:
“PULL UP” – “TERRAIN AHEAD PULL UP” – “OBSTACLE AHEAD PULL UP” – “AVOID TERRAIN” – “AVOID OBSTACLE”
Simultaneously:
Pull to full backstick and maintain in that position
DO NOT CHANGE CONFIGURATION (SLATS/FLAPS, GEAR) UNTIL CLEAR OF OBSTACLE.
Always follow RA orders, even if this results in crossing the intruder altitude, because these orders ensure the best altitude separation.
CAUTION Be aware that the intruder may have a TCAS, and may maneuver in response to a coordinated RA order. Therefore, not following an RA order could compromise safe separation.
If the AP/FD TCAS mode is available:
The flight crew applies this procedure, when a RA triggered, and the AP/FD TCAS mode is engaged. The AP/FD TCAS mode follows the RA orders.
All RA, except any CLIMB RA during approach in CONF 3 or FULL:
If the AP is OFF:
The AP can be engaged
If a preventative RA was triggered: Check that the vertical speed remains out of the red areas of the vertical speed scale.
If a corrective RA was triggered: Check that the vertical speed remains out of the red area, and remains in the green area of the vertical speed scale.

CAUTION If for any reason during a RA, the aircraft vertical speed does not reach the green area of the vertical speed scale, the Pilot Flying (PF) should disconnect the AP, and override the FD orders, in order to lead the aircraft vertical speed out of the red area of the vertical speed scale. If necessary, the PF must use the full speed range between Vαmax and Vmax.
Any CLIMB RA during approach in CONF 3 or FULL:
The AP/FD TCAS mode disengages (the AP/FD no longer follows the RA orders). Follow the SRS GA mode.
Check that the vertical speed remains out of the red area of the vertical speed scale and take over if necessary.
Respect stall, GPWS or windshear warnings.
When the “CLEAR OF CONFLICT” aural alert sounds:
The AP/FD TCAS mode, if engaged, disengages
The flight crew should engage and appropriate vertical mode, or adjust the vertical speed target, in accordance with the latest ATC clearance.
The flight crew should adjust the speed target, and revert to managed speed, as appropriate.
If the AP/FD TCAS mode is not available:
The flight crew must apply this procedure, when a RA is triggered and the AP/FD TCAS mode does not engage.
All RA, except CLIMB RA during approach in CONF 3 or FULL:
Respond promptly and smoothly.
Adjusting or maintain the vertical speed as required, to reach the green area and/or avoid the red area of the vertical speed scale.

Note: Avoid excessive maneuvers while attempting to maintain the vertical speed just outside the red area of the vertical speed scale, and within the green area. If necessary, use the full speed range between Vαmax and Vmax.
Any CLIMB RA during approach in CONF 3 or FULL:
Follow the SRS GA mode.
Check that the vertical speed remains out of the red area of the vertical speed scale and take over if necessary.
Respect stall, GPWS or windshear warnings.
When the “CLEAR OF CONFLICT” aural alert sounds:
Adjust the lateral and vertical guidance to resume normal navigation, in accordance with ATC clearance.
If necessary, reengage the AP/FD.
If windshear is detected, both PFDs display a WINDSHEAR message. An associated aural WINDSHEAR alert sounds three times.
If the flight crew detects WINDSHEAR, apply the following recovery technique:
Takeoff:
Takeoff:
If before V1:

items.challenge: If there are significant variations in airspeed, and in airspeed trend below the indicated V1, reject the takeoff.

items.text: If windshear occurs during the takeoff roll, the aircraft may reach V1 later (or sooner) than expected. The flight crew should ensure that there is sufficient runway remaining to stop the aircraft, if necessary.
If after V1:
If necessary, the flight crew may pull the sidestick fully back.
NOTE: If the FD bars are not displayed, move toward an initial pitch attitude of 17.5 °. Then, if necessary, to prevent a loss in altitude, increase the pitch attitude.
Airborne, initial climb or landing:
If necessary the flight crew may pull the sidestick fully back.

NOTE: 1. Autopilot disengages if the angle of attack value goes above alpha prot. 2. If the FD bars are not displayed, move toward an initial pitch attitude of 17.5 °. Then, if necessary, to prevent a loss in altitude, increase the pitch attitude.
DO NOT CHANGE CONFIGURATION (SLATS/FLAPS, GEAR) UNTIL OUT OF WINDSHEAR. CLOSELY MONITOR FLIGHT PATH AND SPEED. RECOVER SMOOTHLY TO NORMAL CLIMB OUT OF WINDSHEAR.
